To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the association between CPP expression and pSer845-GLU1 in nucleus accumben (NAc) is diet specific, and is mediated by the Ca2+-per-meable AMPARs.
the association between pSer845 and CPP is localized to the NAc core, and the more robust CPP of food-restricted rats may be due to upregulation of pSer845.

cocaine CPP is associated with elevated AMPAR levels and phosphorylation of AMPAR GluA1 Ser845 in NAc core of rats maintained on ad libitum (AL) or food restriction (FR); and that the CPP of FR rats is associated with higher levels of AMPAR Glua1 Ser845 phosphorylation following CPP testing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how dietary conditions influence the neurobiology of cocaine CPP and suggests that NASPM could be a useful therapeutic target for cocaine use disorders.
the role of NAc core AMPARs in the expression of cocaine CPP.
the neurobiological mechanisms that underlie the development and maintenance of cocaine-induced behavioral sensitization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more robust CPP of food restricted rats may result from an upregulation of cocaine induced pSer845-GLUA1.
AMPA receptors in the NAc core are involved in cocaine-conditioned preference in both ad libitum fed and restricted diet rats.
the more robust CPP of food-restricted rats may result from an upregulation of cocaine-induced pSer845 in NAc core.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMPA receptors in the NAc core, especially Ca2+-per-meable AMPARs, are involved in the expression of cocaine CPP.
AMPA receptor phosphorylation in NAc core plays a role in cocaine CPP expression under different dietary conditions.
pSer845-GLUA1 in NAC core is a marker for cocaine reward and that this marker is upregulated by food restriction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pSer845-GLUA1 in NAC core underlies expression in cocaine CPP and does by stabilizing or traffic Ca2+-permissive AMPARs to synaptical membrane.
the role for NAc AMPARs in CPP expression may not be limited to FR rats, and thus the use of FR rats as a model for drug reward may be unwarranted.
the diet switch enhances CPP expression, but not the correlation with AMPA receptor phosphorylation.
